detail: CC0 1874 watercolor, accession 2000.597, native file DP228289, shows the temple, gateway and lower terrace.
Original public-domain Félix Teynard photograph dates to 1851–52, printed 1853–54, and shows the complete standing sequence above the rocky slope.
ETH-Bibliothek Zürich explicitly labels the original 1822 survey edition Public Domain Mark. Plates 23–25 show the measured plan, portico perspective, longitudinal section and side elevation.
The museum measures the main temple at about 43 by 21 feet and 16 feet to roof. It documents Nubian sandstone, the historic terrace and the sole preserved screen wall.
Blackman measured the temple as about 13⅓ by 7 m in 1911, reported the gateway about 10 m from the front and identified the off-axis rock-cut chamber and the eastern terrace about 3½ m high.
The temple and gateway were removed before the modern aswan reservoir submerged the original context.
The museum reports the original terrace as lying beneath almost 200 feet of current water.
